content_units: 4-Month Transition Strategy for Dublin Project Coordinator Roles

For this profile, the   most realistic path   is not “jump straight to Project Manager,” but to position for   Junior Project Coordinator, PMO Coordinator, Project Support Officer, Operations Project Coordinator, Implementation Coordinator, or Customer Operations/Change Coordinator   roles.
- 5 years in customer support operations already proves   cross-team coordination, escalation handling, process ownership, reporting, and stakeholder communication
- These map well to   project coordination fundamentals
- The main gap is   formal PM framing  , not capability
Compensation target of   €42,000+ in Dublin   is achievable for the right junior coordination roles, especially in:
Role Type   Fit Level   Why It Fits   Likely Salary Range in Dublin   Notes
Junior Project Coordinator     High     Strong overlap with tracking tasks, meeting follow-ups, stakeholder updates, documentation     €40k–€48k     Best primary target
PMO Coordinator / PMO Analyst     High     Excel, reporting, status tracking, governance, documentation are relevant     €42k–€50k     Very strong if resume is metrics-led
Project Support Officer     High     Admin + coordination-heavy roles suit support ops background     €38k–€46k     Good stepping-stone
Implementation Coordinator     High     Customer-facing coordination experience transfers well     €42k–€52k     Great option for SaaS firms
Operations Project Coordinator     High     Process improvement and service ops experience are valuable     €42k–€50k     Strong match
Change/Transformation Coordinator   Medium   Good if process documentation and training experience are strong     €40k–€48k     Needs examples of rollout support
These roles are the best balance of:
Resume Repositioning That Will Make the Biggest Difference
The resume should not read like a support profile trying to “switch careers.” It should read like an   operations professional already doing project coordination work  .

Option 1: Resume headline   Project Coordinator / PMO Coordinator candidate with 5 years in customer support operations, stakeholder communication, reporting, process documentation, and cross-functional delivery support

Option 2: Professional summary   Emphasize coordination of initiatives, reporting, escalations, workflow improvements, SOP creation, and collaboration with product/ops teams   Best for PMO and internal project support

Option 3: Experience reframing   Rewrite support bullets into project-style outcomes: tracked actions, managed stakeholders, improved processes, documented workflows, supported rollouts   Best impact on interviews
Option 4: Skills section   Group into PM-relevant buckets: coordination, reporting, documentation, analysis, tools   Best for ATS matching
What to highlight on the resume
- Coordinated cross-functional issues across support, product, operations, and engineering
- Managed stakeholder communications and case updates
- Produced weekly/monthly performance reports in Excel
- Documented SOPs, workflows, process maps, and knowledge base content
- Tracked issue resolution timelines, risks, blockers, and escalations
- Used ticketing systems to prioritize work and monitor throughput
- Applied basic SQL for reporting, trend analysis, or issue investigation
- Coordinated resolution of complex customer and operational issues across support, product, and engineering teams, improving turnaround time by X%
- Maintained action trackers and status updates for service improvement initiatives involving multiple stakeholders
- Created and updated SOPs and workflow documentation to standardize team processes and reduce handling errors by X%
- Built Excel reports and dashboards to track ticket volumes, SLA performance, escalation trends, and operational risks
- Supported rollout of new workflows, internal tools, or policy changes through documentation, testing, and team communication
- Analyzed recurring issue trends using Excel and basic SQL to identify improvement opportunities
What to Learn First to Become Interview-Ready Fast
Do not start with PMP. For a 4-month transition, the best return comes from   practical junior PM tools + one recognized foundation credential  .
- otherwise Asana, Jira, Monday, Trello, Smartsheet fundamentals
- enough to interview confidently with tech employers
- only enough to avoid being weak in interviews
-   CAPM   if they can study seriously and want stronger PM signaling
-   Google Project Management Certificate first   for speed and practicality
- Add   CAPM later   only if needed
- milestone tracker / project plan in Excel
- SOP or process improvement document from prior experience, anonymized
This helps prove “I can already do coordinator work.”
Month 1   Reframe profile   Rewrite CV; update LinkedIn headline; map support work to project language; identify 30 target employers   PM-focused CV + target list
Month 2   Build proof   Complete PM fundamentals course; create tracker/status report samples; practice STAR stories   Portfolio pack + interview stories
Month 3   Apply strategically   Apply to 8–15 roles/week; target recruiters; tailor CV to PMO/project/implementation roles   Active pipeline of interviews
Month 4   Convert interviews   Mock interviews; improve salary pitch; address PM-title gap confidently; expand to adjacent roles   Offer-ready interview performance
How to Explain the Career Transition in Interviews

“I’ve spent the last 5 years in customer support operations, where a big part of my role was coordinating cross-functional work, managing stakeholders, tracking issues, improving processes, and documenting workflows. That naturally moved me toward project-based work, and I’m now targeting junior project coordination roles where I can bring that operational delivery experience into a formal project environment.”
- avoids apologizing for lack of PM title
- makes the move feel like a   continuation  , not a reinvention
For a junior move,   €42,000   is realistic but should be handled carefully.
- target roles advertised in the   €40k–€50k   zone
- present expectation as   “targeting roles in the low-to-mid 40s depending on scope, benefits, and growth path”
- avoid sounding fixed on title over scope
